<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
# Game reset. Try different approach - click purple objects instead
seg = current_frame.segmentation
nodes = seg['nodes']

# Find purple objects (not the HUD bar at bottom)
purple_objects = [n for n in nodes if n['color'] == 'p']
print(f"Purple objects: {len(purple_objects)}")
for n in purple_objects:
    boundary = n['boundary']
    rows = [p[0] for p in boundary]
    cols = [p[1] for p in boundary]
    print(f"  boundary={boundary}, rows={min(rows)}-{max(rows)}, cols={min(cols)}-{max(cols)}")

# The HUD bar is at row 63, so exclude that
purple_gameplay = [n for n in purple_objects if min(p[0] for p in n['boundary']) < 60]
print(f"Gameplay purple objects: {len(purple_gameplay)}")

# Try clicking on purple objects
clicks = []
for n in purple_gameplay:
    boundary = n['boundary']
    rows = [p[0] for p in boundary]
    cols = [p[1] for p in boundary]
    center_row = (min(rows) + max(rows)) // 2
    center_col = (min(cols) + max(cols)) // 2
    clicks.append({'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': center_row, 'col': center_col})

print(f"Clicking {len(clicks)} purple objects")
action(clicks)
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
